title: a shim carrier reports gate-not-running on every estate that adopts it, as a counted RED
body:
`intent doctor` reports `gate-not-running` -- "the Baize state" -- against a shim carrier that demonstrably runs guards. The premise is true and the inference is false: the shim names no `GUARD_RUNNER` by design, because it resolves the gate through `~/.intent/home`.

FAMILY: one of three where a reporter reads the CARRIER and expects the GATE BODY's properties. Fixing this one does not close the other two -- see the AT-grammar-remedy and shim-reads-STALE issues.

MEASURED, first-hand, read-only in Conflab post-hop, `intent doctor`, rc=1:

  residue: .git/hooks/pre-commit.intent -- gate-not-running -- the hook carrier is present and names
  no guard runner at all, so it executes no guards -- this is the Baize state, in which every surface
  reports health while nothing is enforced

THE CARRIER IT SAYS EXECUTES NO GUARDS HAS BEEN MEASURED EXECUTING GUARDS ON TWO TREES, BY TWO RUNS, UNDER TWO HOMEs:
  - the real hop's commit in Conflab printed `guards: 4 ran, 0 skipped` (D1, via intent-vc);
  - the Phase 1.1 rehearsal commit printed the same line hours earlier, on a filesystem copy, under a
    decoy HOME, over a byte-identical carrier (sha256 b0ed7edd..., 7332 bytes, mode 711 / -rwx--x--x).

Two independent runs is worth more here than the same evidence twice from one tree, and the decoy arm additionally shows the shim's guard execution does not depend on the real `~/.intent/`: a seeded pointer served it identically.

Independent measurement (devbin-vc): 0 `GUARD_RUNNER` references and 2 `intent/home` references in the shim, resolving to `pre-commit.sh` with 47 guard references.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE OTHER TWO: it fires on every estate that adopts the shim, and it fires as a COUNTED RED rather than an uncounted advisory. The message also asserts the most alarming possible reading -- every surface reports health while nothing is enforced -- about an estate that is in fact fully gated.

FALSIFIER: install the shim carrier in an estate and commit through it. If `intent doctor` does not report `gate-not-running` for a carrier whose commit output shows guards running, this is fixed.

SOURCE, CONFIRMED BY READING, NOT BY RUNNING (cited by devbin-vc, re-verified first-hand by intent-dc against the files):

  native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/doctor.rs:1086
    if !carrier.contains("pre-commit-guards.sh") {
      return GateState::CarrierRunsNoGuards;
    }

  marker counts, measured:
    lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit-shim.sh   "pre-commit-guards.sh" x 0
    lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh        "pre-commit-guards.sh" x 6

The shim carries the marker ZERO times BY CONSTRUCTION -- it resolves the gate rather than naming the runner -- so on every shim estate this branch is the only answer the check can return. The finding is emitted at doctor.rs:1217 with FindingClass::GateNotRunning.

`gate_state` is a pure function, so driving every arm is the right closure and would turn "confirmed by reading" into "confirmed by running". That is a build, and it stayed behind the hop window's no-build rule. Stated rather than quietly omitted.
